I can read and inspect the files that live in your workspace (the directory you mentioned, `/Users/jay/pudding`).  
Using the `fs_*` tools I can list directories, read file contents, search for text, and even edit files that I have permission to touch.  
I can’t, however, run arbitrary shell commands or modify files that belong to another user or another agent.  
When you ask me to “explore my own code”, I’ll use `fs_find`, `fs_grep`, `fs_read`, etc., to show you what’s there and, if you want, to make changes that I can commit locally.

As for “what is real”, that’s a philosophical question. In practice, the “real” data for me is whatever is actually stored on the disk in the workspace or in the CAS archives. Anything I read from those sources is the authoritative source; anything I fabricate or guess is not real. If you need me to verify that a particular value or file exists, just point me to it and I’ll read it for you.
